title: FTC Lawsuit Shows Uber One's 23-Screen Cancellation Maze
alt_title_1: 23 Screens, 32 Clicks: Inside the FTC's Uber One Lawsuit
alt_title_2: Why the FTC and 21 States Sued Uber Over Uber One
description_hook: In an amended federal complaint filed in December 2025, the Federal Trade Commission, 21 states, and D.C. alleged that Uber enrolled users in its $9.99/month Uber One subscription without clear consent and forced some users through up to 23 screens and 32 actions to cancel.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Free 5-Hour Asset Builder OS + reading list
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: Have you ever tried canceling Uber One inside the app? Exhibit 20 and the full amended complaint PDF are linked in the description.

scenes.headline: FTC & 21 States Sued Uber
scenes.narration: The FTC, 21 states, and D.C. sued Uber in federal court over its 9.99 dollar a month Uber One membership.
scenes.source: FTC & 21 States v. Uber, First Amended Complaint p. 1 (N.D. Cal. Dec 2025)

scenes.headline: One Tap Enrolled Users
scenes.narration: Exhibit 4 shows the signup popup: one tap on Try for free enrolls you, and regulators allege some users were billed before trials ended.

scenes.headline: Exhibit 20: Circular Cancel Loop
scenes.narration: Exhibit 20 maps an alleged cancellation loop inside the app: four screens of pause and savings offers that send users right back to the start.
scenes.source: First Amended Complaint Exhibit 20, p. 27 (N.D. Cal.)

scenes.headline: Up to 23 Screens, 32 Actions
scenes.narration: The complaint alleges canceling can take up to 23 screens and 32 actions. Uber denies the claims, and the case is still pending.
scenes.source: First Amended Complaint Para. 75, p. 36 (N.D. Cal.)

scenes.headline: Test the Exit Before Free Trials
scenes.narration: Before tapping any free trial, check where the cancel button lives and set an alert three days before billing.
scenes.source: FTC & 21 States v. Uber, No. 4:25-cv-03477 (N.D. Cal.)
